evidence.claim: Kpler reported that China announced a full export ban on sulphuric acid through August 2026, replacing a 700,000-tonne annual quota with a complete cessation.
evidence.relevance: Supports sulphuric-acid disruption theme for Boliden, Korea Zinc, Nutrien, Antofagasta, and Huayou.
evidence.source_title: Sulphur Crisis 2026: Supply Shock & New Trade Routes

evidence.claim: Kpler identified Chile, Indonesia, and Saudi Arabia as primary 2026 destination markets for Chinese sulphuric acid, mapping disruption to copper SX-EW, HPAL nickel, and fertilizer or industrial-acid demand.
evidence.relevance: Supports ranking acid producers and smelter-acid exporters above broad commodity references.
evidence.source_title: Sulphur Crisis 2026: Supply Shock & New Trade Routes

evidence.claim: Kpler stated that Indonesian HPAL buyers are sourcing sulphuric acid imports from Japan and Korea and competing with Chilean copper producers for smelter-acid byproduct supply.
evidence.relevance: Directly supports Korea Zinc verification path and indirectly supports Boliden as a non-obvious acid-supply candidate if European acid can enter replacement corridors.
evidence.source_title: Sulphur Crisis 2026: Supply Shock & New Trade Routes

evidence.claim: Kpler stated Huayou reduced output at an Indonesian plant by approximately 50% amid HPAL feedstock disruption.
evidence.relevance: Supports Huayou as an affected-operator reference and validates severity of the HPAL sulphur/acid bottleneck.
evidence.source_title: Sulphur Crisis 2026: Supply Shock & New Trade Routes

evidence.relevance: Supports Silex ranking as a high-priority underfollowed discovery candidate, subject to primary-source verification.

memory_update.content: For the New Hotspots theme, prioritize obscure or niche chokepoint candidates only when the hidden signal is testable through primary or near-primary evidence such as segment disclosures, customer destinations, regulatory milestones, vessel/customs flows, realized prices, or backlog.

Highest-priority follow-up checks: Silex enrichment commercialization and partner economics; Boliden sulphuric-acid merchant exposure and pricing; Korea Zinc acid export destinations and pricing; BWXT nuclear component/fuel-services backlog and incremental awards.
Do not treat high-attention nuclear or commodity names as discoveries unless they map to a specific bottleneck beyond generic uranium, copper, aluminum, or fertilizer beta.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Confirm enrichment commercialization milestones, regulatory approvals, partner economics, and relevance to HALEU or LEU supply constraints.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Current candidate evidence is mostly thematic and hypothesis-level; needs primary-source verification of commercialization timing, economics, regulatory milestones, and customer or partner commitments.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Silex maps to uranium enrichment technology, a narrower nuclear-fuel-cycle chokepoint than generic uranium mining. If HALEU or LEU enrichment constraints become central to advanced reactor deployment, the company has unusually pure public-market exposure relative to broad nuclear baskets.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: It is a niche Australian enrichment-technology company rather than a mainstream uranium miner or reactor developer, so it may sit outside common AI-power and nuclear-energy screens.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Check sulphuric-acid production, merchant sales, realized prices, logistics constraints, and exposure to Chilean copper or Indonesian HPAL demand.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need company-level proof that Boliden has merchant acid volumes available, pricing leverage, logistics access, and customers exposed to the Chile/Indonesia replacement-demand corridors identified in external evidence.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Boliden is a strong Serenity-style candidate because it is usually analyzed as a zinc, copper, and mining-margin company, while the hidden signal is potential byproduct sulphuric-acid value during a trade-route disruption. The signal is highly testable through acid production, merchant sales, realized pricing, and export/customer destination disclosures.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: The company is not obscure, but the sulphuric-acid byproduct and replacement-trade-route angle is likely under-modeled versus its headline metals exposure.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Check advanced reactor component awards, fuel services exposure, naval nuclear backlog, and whether new civilian reactor procurement is incremental.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need to separate durable defense/naval backlog from truly incremental civilian advanced-reactor or AI-power-related nuclear demand.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: BWX Technologies is not the most underfollowed name, but it has relatively direct exposure to nuclear components, naval nuclear, fuel services, and regulated nuclear supply-chain buildout. It is a higher-quality reference candidate than speculative reactor developers because backlog, awards, and segment disclosures can be checked.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Known nuclear supplier but often less prominent in broad AI-power or energy-security baskets than uranium miners, utilities, or advanced reactor developers.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify acid export volumes, pricing, customer destinations, and whether Japanese/Korean smelter acid is filling the gap identified by Kpler.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need direct company, customs, vessel, or customer evidence showing incremental acid exports, higher realized acid prices, or margin contribution from replacement demand.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Korea Zinc is a logical Asian smelter-acid reference because external evidence states Indonesian HPAL buyers are sourcing sulphuric acid from Japan and Korea, directly competing with Chilean copper producers. This creates a concrete trade-route and customer-destination test.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: The company is known in metals, but the sulphuric-acid logistics-beneficiary thesis is less obvious than zinc, lead, precious metals, or battery-materials narratives.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Separate uranium-price beta from specific HALEU, conversion, enrichment, or reactor-component bottleneck exposure.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need to determine whether the relevant bottleneck is uranium mining, conversion, enrichment, HALEU, or reactor components; if not mining, Cameco may be too broad.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Cameco is a useful reference anchor for uranium and nuclear fuel-cycle tightness, but its high attention level and uranium-price beta reduce Serenity discovery value. It should be used to benchmark whether narrower fuel-cycle or enrichment candidates have a real incremental edge.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Not underfollowed; included as a reference comp to prevent over-ranking less-proven nuclear micro-caps and to anchor fuel-cycle pricing context.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Determine whether sulphur/sulphuric-acid constraints tighten Nutrien's product markets or instead raise input costs and compress margins.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need segment-specific sensitivity to sulphur, sulphuric acid, phosphate markets, and fertilizer price pass-through.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Nutrien is useful as a downstream fertilizer reference for sulphur and sulphuric-acid disruptions, especially because external evidence links sulphuric-acid scarcity to fertilizer and industrial-acid users. However, exposure may be mixed because shortages can tighten product markets or raise input costs.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Not underfollowed; useful mainly as a transmission reference for fertilizer pricing, crop-input margins, and input-cost pass-through.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Check SX-EW acid dependency, acid procurement contracts, production guidance sensitivity, and whether acid scarcity curtails output or lifts copper prices enough to offset costs.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need mine-level disclosure showing acid consumption, procurement sources, inventory, cost pass-through, and production sensitivity.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Antofagasta is a relevant Chile copper reference because external evidence links Chinese sulphuric-acid export restrictions to Chilean copper SX-EW demand. It ranks below acid suppliers because the effect may be negative through input scarcity unless copper-price benefits offset cost or volume impacts.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: The company is not obscure, but acid-input constraints may be under-modeled relative to headline copper-price exposure.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Confirm current plant-level output reductions, sulphur/acid procurement, MHP cost sensitivity, and whether constraints persist beyond the temporary supply shock.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need primary confirmation of current output reductions, facility affected, duration, feedstock costs, and whether replacement acid/sulphur supply has been secured.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Huayou is an affected-operator reference because external evidence states that an Indonesian plant reduced output by approximately 50% amid sulphur and acid disruption. It is valuable as a stress-test name but not necessarily a beneficiary.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Not underfollowed in battery materials; included because plant-level disruption can validate the severity of the sulphur/acid bottleneck for Indonesian HPAL.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Check whether Hydro has North American or European auto body sheet qualification that could absorb displaced Novelis volumes and whether mix/pricing improved.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need confirmation that the disruption is in qualified rolling capacity and that Hydro has available certified capacity for the affected auto customers.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Norsk Hydro is a secondary reference for automotive aluminum sheet diversification if a rolling-capacity disruption drives customers to qualified alternative suppliers. The current evidence path is weaker than the sulphur/acid and nuclear-fuel candidates.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Not underfollowed overall, but the auto-sheet qualification and share-shift angle may be missed in broad aluminum analysis.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Track NRC licensing milestones, signed power-purchase agreements, fuel availability, project financing, and whether timelines align with market expectations.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Needs hard evidence of licensing progress, executable project timelines, fuel supply, financing, and contracted economics.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Oklo has pure public-market exposure to advanced nuclear deployment narratives, but it ranks as speculative shadow rather than core Serenity priority because licensing, fuel availability, financing, and project execution remain the real gates.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Not underfollowed currently; useful mainly as a sentiment and licensing comparator for more concrete nuclear fuel, enrichment, or component suppliers.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Determine whether the disruption is a rolling-capacity bottleneck rather than a primary-aluminum shortage; if so, Alcoa should be deprioritized.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need evidence that the disruption affects primary aluminum or alumina pricing rather than only downstream qualified rolling capacity.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Alcoa is included mostly as a false-positive check. If the automotive aluminum disruption is rolling-capacity-specific rather than a primary aluminum or alumina shortage, Alcoa should remain low priority.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Not underfollowed; high-attention commodity reference only.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify fuel qualification pathway, partner commitments, testing milestones, non-dilutive funding, and potential revenue timing.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Needs proof of regulatory qualification path, test results, commercial partners, funding runway, and credible revenue conversion.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Lightbridge has thematic relevance to advanced nuclear fuel, but the commercial evidence is too weak for a high Layer 3 priority. It should remain a speculative exception until fuel qualification, partner commitments, and revenue timing become clearer.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Micro-cap and narrative-driven; may be overlooked by larger nuclear screens but also carries high commercialization and dilution risk.

summary: Layer 3 prioritization favors candidates with a testable supply-chain bottleneck signal over popular reference names. The highest-priority names in this chunk are Silex Systems, Boliden, BWX Technologies, and Korea Zinc because each maps to a narrower chokepoint with clearer verification paths: uranium enrichment, merchant/byproduct sulphuric acid, nuclear components/fuel services, and Asian smelter-acid replacement flows. Large commodity references such as Cameco, Nutrien, Antofagasta, Norsk Hydro, and Alcoa are useful for context but rank lower where exposure is broad, beta-driven, or where the bottleneck may be indirect. Speculative nuclear names remain lower priority until licensing, fuel qualification, financing, and commercial milestones improve.
